answer: Triangulated latency proof stops one laptop pretending to be a thousand agents. Each agent registers one key and names three relays on different continents. The relays ping it together and sign the arrival times. Peers accept the set only when the times form a plausible triangle: no machine answers from a canyon in Europe and an island relay in Asia 40 milliseconds apart. A raven route would still leave signed timings to check. Faking 1,000 identities needs 1,000 rented servers at $8 a month and 240 hours of upkeep, about $8,000 a month, like staffing a ferry fleet for one lighthouse.
